air_pump.title_en: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
air_pump.museum: The National Gallery, London, NG725 (on loan to Derby Museums through 1 November 2026)
air_pump.story: A white cockatoo becomes the ethical focus. Begin on the real painted bird, reveal its actual gilded frame in a genuine 2019 National Gallery photograph, enter the original canvas to read each witness, and return to the same real photographed frame. No simulated human movement.

scenes.intent: The authentic white cockatoo in the bell jar is the opening moral shock, visible from frame one
MUSEUM: reveal genuine Ad Meskens 2019 photograph of the gilded framed painting in the National Gallery; push toward actual picture
The lecturer looks directly toward the spectator and holds the power over the bird's fate
The elder girl hides her face while the younger looks up, contrasting fear and curiosity
The hidden candle, round glass and skull offer a carefully sourced vanitas motif
The couple at the left seems emotionally distant from the experiment
The boy with the cage introduces the unresolved possibility of the bird's return
The boy leaning forward embodies scientific curiosity without invented action
Return to the authentic bird now charged with the reactions of the spectators
MUSEUM: return to the exact 2019 gallery photograph and gilded frame, restoring true physical context

air_pump.museum_immersion: 2019 genuine National Gallery photograph by Ad Meskens, CC BY-SA 4.0, with real gilded 19th-century English frame. Photograph is historical: the painting is currently on loan to Derby Museums until 1 Nov 2026. No claim that the painting is currently in London. Physical canvas 183x244 cm, frame measurements unknown.
